### Isabella Bank Corporation Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Earnings


October 29, 2026


**MOUNT PLEASANT, MI /[ACCESS Newswire](https://www.accessnewswire.com/) / October 29, 2026 /** Isabella Bank Corporation (Nasdaq:ISBA) ("Isabella" or the "Company") reported net income of $6.6 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, for the third quarter 2026 compared to $5.2 million, or $0.71 per diluted share, for the third quarter 2025.


**THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS**


- Record net income of $6.6 million, which included after-tax expenses of $657,000 related to the proposed acquisition of Grand River Commerce, Inc.
- Net interest margin (NIM) improved to 3.71%, up from 3.15% in third quarter 2025
- All required regulatory and shareholder approvals received to complete the Grand River acquisition, which is expected to close on November 2, 2026, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions


"Isabella Bank Corporation reported a record quarter of net income, supported by continued expansion in our net interest margin," said President and CEO Jerome Schwind. "We are pleased with the increase in deposit balances, which further strengthens the Corporation's funding position. Overall, the quarter reflected positive earnings momentum.


"We also have received required regulatory and shareholder approvals to complete the acquisition of Grand River Commerce and Grand River Bank," Schwind added. "This is a key milestone and the transaction is on track for our anticipated November 2, 2026 close. Importantly, this merger supports our disciplined growth strategy by expanding our customer base and presence in West Michigan. We are keenly focused on a smooth integration and clear communication with customers and employees to assure continued strong customer service."


**FINANCIAL CONDITION** *(September 30, 2026 to December 31, 2025 comparison)*


Total assets increased $31.1 million, or 1.4%, to $2.2 billion as of September 30, 2026. This increase was primarily due to an increase of $112.5 million in cash and cash equivalents, offset by an $88.3 million decline in available-for-sale (AFS) securities.


The AFS securities portfolio decreased $88.3 million, or 17.7%, to $409.5 million as of September 30, 2026. The decrease was a result of maturities and principal paydowns of $177.1 million, offset by $100.7 million in purchases. Net unrealized losses on AFS securities were $21.7 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $9.9 million at December 31, 2025. Net unrealized losses as a percentage of the amortized cost of AFS securities increased to 5.0%, compared to 1.9% at December 31, 2025.


Loans decreased $556,000 to $1.5 billion as of September 30, 2026. The commercial real estate and residential real estate loan portfolios grew $29.9 million and $29.7 million, respectively, but were offset by declines in advances to mortgage brokers and consumer loans of $39.0 million and $10.6 million, respectively. Most residential originations were adjustable-rate products, which are retained on the balance sheet rather than sold in the secondary market. The consumer loan portfolio continues to decrease amid declining demand, continued competition, and disciplined adherence to credit quality standards.


The allowance for credit losses (ACL) increased $671,000, or 4.9%, to $14.4 million as of September 30, 2026. The increase is due to loan growth and an increase in loss rates driven by loans charged off during the year. Nonaccrual loans were $7.5 million as of September 30, 2026 compared to $4.6 million at December 31, 2025. Past due and accruing accounts between 30 to 89 days as a percentage of total loans was 0.10% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.44% at year-end 2025.


Total deposits increased $73.0 million, or 4.0%, to $1.9 billion as of September 30, 2026. The increase was a result of a $141.8 million increase in money market accounts and a $11.1 million increase in savings deposits. These increases were offset by a $51.3 million decline in certificates of deposit, a $16.6 million decline in noninterest bearing demand deposits, and a $12.1 million decline in interest bearing demand deposits.


Total equity was $245.6 million, or $32.09 per share, at September 30, 2026 compared to $231.4 million, or $31.60 per share, as of December 31, 2025. The increase in total equity is primarily due to the issuance of 322,685 shares as part of the ongoing at-the-market stock offering, increasing total equity by $12.5 million, net of expenses. Tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) was $25.78 as of September 30, 2026, compared to $25.01 as of December 31, 2025. Net unrealized losses in the AFS securities portfolio reduced tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) by $2.26 and $1.09 for the respective periods.


**RESULTS OF OPERATIONS** *(for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, unless otherwise noted)*


Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.6 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, compared with $5.2 million, or $0.71 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $16.6 million, or $2.24 per diluted share, compared with $14.2 million, or $1.92 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 included after-tax merger-related expenses of $657,000 and $1.1 million, respectively.


Net interest income was $19.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and $16.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing 3.71% and 3.15% of interest earning assets, or NIM on a fully tax equivalent basis (non-GAAP), respectively. The book yield from securities was 3.20% and 2.42% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The yield on loans increased to 5.95% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 5.78% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in loan yields was primarily due to higher rates on new loans and variable rate commercial loans that continue to reprice. The cost of interest-bearing liabilities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased to 2.08% from 2.25% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to lower rates on money market and certificate of deposit products.


Net interest income was $54.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and $45.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing 3.53% and 3.12% of earning assets, or NIM on a fully tax equivalent basis (non-GAAP), respectively. The book yield from securities was 2.83% and 2.34% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The yield on loans increased to 5.88% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from 5.75% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in loan yields was primarily due to higher rates on new loans and variable rate commercial loans that continue to reprice. The cost of interest-bearing liabilities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased to 2.10% from 2.25% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to lower rates on money market and certificate of deposit products.


The provision for credit losses was $50,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as a result of net charge offs totaling $207,000, offset by an $81,000 decrease in the ACL on loans and a decrease in the reserve for unfunded commitments. The provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was $209,000, which reflects a $172,000 increase in the ACL and net charge offs totaling $74,000, offset by a decrease in the reserve for unfunded commitments.


The provision for credit losses was $1.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to a credit of $1.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net charge offs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $844,000, while there were net recoveries of $1.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $4.6 million and $4.3 million, respectively. Service charges and fees increased $202,000 and wealth management fees increased $94,000 due to growth in assets under management since second quarter 2025.


Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $13.3 million and $11.5 million, respectively. Service charges and fees increased $1.1 million, wealth management fees increased $355,000 due to growth in assets under management, and earnings on bank-owned life insurance (BOLI) policies increased $220,000 due to additional investments in a separate account BOLI. Other noninterest income included gains of $137,000 and $163,000 related to death benefits from BOLI policies for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.


Noninterest expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $15.6 million and $14.0 million, respectively. Compensation and benefit expenses increased $867,000, reflecting annual merit increases, incentives, and higher medical insurance claims. Occupancy and equipment increased $156,000 and merger-related expenses were $672,000.


Noninterest expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 were $45.7 million and $41.0 million, respectively. Compensation and benefit expenses increased $2.1 million for the same reasons as the quarterly comparison. Occupancy and equipment expenses increased $636,000 and merger-related expenses were $1.2 million.


Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $1.6 million and $1.0 million, respectively. The effective tax rate (ETR) for the same periods was 20% and 17%, respectively. Income tax expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $3.8 million and $3.1 million, respectively. The ETR was 18% for both the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The ETR in the first nine months of 2026 included the impact of certain non-deductible merger-related expenses. The ETR in the first nine months of 2025 included a one-time tax expense related to the lifetime earnings on BOLI policies that were surrendered.


**About Isabella Bank Corporation**


Isabella Bank Corporation (Nasdaq: ISBA) is the parent holding company of Isabella Bank, a state-chartered community bank headquartered in Mt. Pleasant, Michigan. Isabella Bank was chartered in 1903 and has been committed to serving its customers' and communities' local banking needs for over 120 years. The Bank offers personal and commercial lending and deposit products, as well as investment, trust, and estate planning services. The Bank has locations throughout eight Mid-Michigan counties: Bay, Clare, Gratiot, Isabella, Mecosta, Midland, Montcalm, and Saginaw.


For more information about Isabella Bank Corporation, visit the Investor Relations link at[www.isabellabank.com](https://pr.report/suzz) .
